methods.identification: The detector names the tool with confidence >= 0.5 on the obfuscated fixture (and, where the fixture records a version, the version it reads equals it). Reported as detected / fixtures.
methods.structure: structureScore(original, recovered): F1 of the multiset of parent>child node-type edges of the two syntax trees; names, literal values, comments, parentheses and sibling order are ignored. 1.0 = the same shape of program. Mean over fixtures whose output parses.
methods.semantic: fidelity(original, recovered): Dice coefficient of the longest common subsequence of the semantic-token streams (node kinds, operators, literal values, locals by order of declaration, globals by name), over the first 6000 tokens of each. Mean over fixtures whose output parses.
methods.runtime: The recovered script and the original program are run on the same real runtime (PUC Lua 5.1 / LuaJIT / Lua 5.4 through lupa, or Luau 0.739) and their captured output compared. Counted only where the obfuscator’s own output behaved like the original, so a tool defect is never charged to the engine. same / judged.
methods.completeness: Both of: residualIndicators(recovered) is empty (the detector finds in the recovered text no tool with unrecoverable evidence, none of the traits state-machine, bytecode-blob, string-table, junk-code, opaque-predicates, escape-encoded-strings, and no virtual machine’s function records and interpreter), and the engine’s own report lists nothing left unresolved. complete / fixtures.
methods.vmConstants: Only for builds that keep the program as VM bytecode and were not lifted: vmConstantsRecall(original, vm.constants), the share of the original’s string literals (two characters or more) that appear among the constants read from the script’s own decryptor, with none of the program run. A profile of the data, not a reconstruction. Mean over VM fixtures.
methods.stability: Wall-clock milliseconds of one recover() call (sandboxed evaluation on) on the reference machine; failures = fixtures whose recovery threw or whose output does not parse.

projects.name: Obscura
researchedFrom: README and git history read as text; the three revisions were then run in tests/corpus/tools/sandbox_run.py (no network, no host files) through gen_obscura.py

Obscura (MIT, Python, vo3pal) is a Luau obfuscator with modes lightweight, rename, native and vm; versions 1.0.0 (pre-hardening), 1.0.1 (2026-04-30, VM hardenin [https://github.com/vo3pal/obscura; high for the history; nothing measured]

versions.note: the state before the VM hardening release (2026-04-29): VM with an encrypted constant pool, --level 1-4, --vm
v1.0.1 (2026-04-30): VM hardening (lazy constants, split keys, integrity checks), --vm-hardening
v1.1.0 (2026-10-08): --mode lightweight/rename/native/vm, rolling bytecode reads by default

improvements.summary: math.floor / math.ceil of an integer literal is the literal (the number layer wraps every number in it), so bit32.bxor(math.floor(a), math.floor(b)) folds and the control-flow flattener's next states become constants
a closure called on the spot that only computes a constant from constants is that constant (the opaque predicates `(function() local n = 22 return n * n < 0 end)()`)
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a closure called on the spot

improvements.summary: a flattened function inside another function's body is unflattened: a leaf that returns or raises the `error("CFF Error: Invalid state")` else no longer counts against the machine, and a loop of two blocks that cannot end on its own is read (closes KNOWN-ISSUES 27 for this shape)
a table of untouched globals read only by constant keys (the table-indirection layer, also `math.pi`) is inlined, whatever its name looks like; a numeric statement nobody keeps (`math.cos(12)`) goes
tests: tests/formats-ix.test.mjs: simplify: a table of builtins

improvements.summary: the run of executor-detection ifs at the top (1.1.0: empty error; 1.0.x: "Security violation" messages, in a do block) is taken off when at least two are present and one probes an executor-only global

lightweight mode decrypts its string table in place (`T[k] = D(T[k], key, i)`): the decoder call is seeded with the stored text, evaluated, and the reads and the copies the obfuscator made (`local a = T[1]`) become the strings
a function that reads or slices a string, mixes it with bxor and builds text with string.char is a decoder from its first call, however it is wrapped (a script with two hidden strings has two calls)
the reference-runtime oracle no longer dies on a recovered file whose report header holds a real Unicode character (it used to take every later request with it)

what is inside a VM that was not lifted: the function records (instruction bytes, parameters, registers), and the constants, read by running only the statements that set them up in the sandbox (never the interpreter); the hardened 1.1.0 build keeps its constants in keyed per-function records, which are opened one record at a time after the set-up loop that salts each record with the hash of its code. Reported in the output header as a profile, never as a recovery

the plain VM build (1.0.1 and 1.1.0) is lifted back to source: every handler of the build's own interpreter is taken apart into the operands it reads and a canonical body (names by first appearance, operands by first use, so a build that shuffles its operand order writes the same text) and recognised against a template list; the program's functions are decoded with the script's own key, boxes become the variables they stand for, byte jumps become instruction jumps, and the Lua 5.1 chunk goes to the decompiler that reads IronBrew 2 and Hercules. Every one of the 13 plain builds reads completely (no handler left unrecognised); where the tool's own output is right the lifted program runs like the original on Luau (7 of 7 in 1.1.0, 2 of 2 in 1.0.1)

failurePatterns.summary: the hardened builds (vm-max, vm-cached; 1.1.0, and 1.0.1 vm-max) are profiled, not lifted: they keep instruction bytes encrypted per function record (rolling PRNG, salted with the hash of the record), choose an operand order and a byte order per operation, dispatch through a tree of range tests instead of a flat chain, and fuse several operations into one generated handler (BLOCKn). The plain vm build is lifted since Prompt XI (improvements/vm-lift)
failurePatterns.evidence: tests/obscura-vm.test.mjs (hardened builds are reported as not lifted); docs/AUDIT.md (vm-max, vm-cached: semantic 2% to 4%, complete 0)

failurePatterns.summary: identifier renaming is not reversible: samples whose original names are descriptive (s02, s03, s06) lose fidelity that no pass can win back; the structure is recovered
failurePatterns.evidence: the remaining differences in s02/s03/s06 are names and inlined named constants

failurePatterns.summary: Obscura 1.0.0 fails with a Lexer error on one sample (s03); recorded as tool-error in its manifest, never counted as a recovery

four of the six 1.0.1 VM outputs (s02, s04, s05, s06) do not behave like the original program even on the reference runtime. s05 shows why: the compiler places a numeric loop's variable one register above where the FORLOOP handler writes it (the lifted program reads an unset register), and the VM itself fails earlier with a different error. The lifted program follows the bytecode; it is not expected to match an output the tool got wrong, and those fixtures are not judged

assumptions: Only the three revisions named were run; earlier history was read, not run
Behaviour is checked on Luau 0.739 (the vendored binary), not in Roblox: `game`, `workspace` and the Roblox API come from the oracle's mock environment

projects.name: Zartha
researchedFrom: README, Main.lua, Pipeline.lua and the Vm tree read as text; run through run_isolated.py with drivers/zartha.lua, which does in memory what Pipeline.lua does (luac replaced by string.dump)

failurePatterns.summary: a per-build Lua 5.1 bytecode VM with generated opcodes: identified (watermark and the `Env["string"]["char"]` prelude) and flagged as not recovered; no lifter was written
luasrcdiet inside the tool fails on s06 in both configurations that minify (an unexpected backslash); recorded as tool-error

on s06 the tool writes `\n\t` as literal characters into the code of one opcode handler, which PUC Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT reject ("unexpected symbol near '\'"); QuickSilver's parser rejects it too, so those outputs are counted as unparsed, not as recovery failures

measured on Lua 5.1 and LuaJIT in an isolated runner with a wall-clock limit: 16 of 54 outputs behave like the original, 8 do not (s01 and s02 in default / minify / encryptstrings / flatten: the compiled program prints a wrong list of primes and nil where the original prints booleans), antitamper stops no run within 15 s, constants and all fail with "attempt to call field ?" (a nil value), and s06 / s08 are rejected by the runtime. None of these is counted against the engine

assumptions: The watermark text is a setting (`File generated using [Zartha]` is the default), so it is evidence and not proof; the prelude rule is the structural one

The tool's own output was NOT run on the reference runtimes (the VM builds did not finish inside the verification budget on lupa, twice); `toolOutputVerified` is 0 for these fixtures, and nothing is claimed about whether the generated VMs reproduce the originals. The one sample whose output PUC 5.1 and LuaJIT reject at parse time (s06) is the only behaviour fact known

backlog.detail: Obscura level-2/3 and LuaXen AST stage; MoonVeil's nested case is unchanged

backlog.item: Luraph files without a version banner (15 of 218)
backlog.state: 11 of 15 identified by structure; 4 remain unidentified
backlog.detail: the 15 files were read one by one: 11 are Luraph 14.x-shaped VMs without their banner (a returned table of short-named handlers with 0X / 0B literals, or the LPH_ build-flag macros) and are now identified by those two structural rules (flagged unrecoverable); the other 4 are not Luraph VMs (two request-function scripts, a hub script, a plain script) and are classified, not identified. Luraph's version still cannot be read without its banner

backlog.item: Per-build bytecode VMs (Obscura VM, Zartha, FusGato, IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm)
backlog.detail: each is flagged unrecoverable so that the report cannot say "recovered"; none has a lifter. Since Prompt X the Obscura VM (all three revisions, plain and hardened) has a profile of its data (functions, instruction bytes, decrypted constants; on all 39 Obscura VM fixtures every string of two or more characters of the original program is among the constants read: recall 1.00, `categories.vmConstants` in the database), shown in the report as NOT lifted

backlog.item: A lifter that rebuilds source from Obscura VM bytecode
backlog.state: plain Obscura VM done; hardened Obscura, Zartha, FusGato, IronBrikked, RealObfuscator vm not started
backlog.detail: the Obscura lifter reads each build's handlers from its own interpreter and decodes with its own key (src/recover/obscura-vm.js). The hardened Obscura builds additionally need: the instruction bytes opened in the sandbox (they are encrypted per record), an operand reader per byte order and offset style, the tree of range tests flattened to its leaves, and the fused BLOCK handlers split back into the operations they were made from. Zartha, FusGato and IronBrikked are different formats and need their own handler readers.

backlog.item: MoonVeil 2.0.26: the table of factories joined into one program
backlog.state: done for 2.0.26; 2.1.0 is a different design
backlog.detail: 2.0.26 does not keep its program as bytecode: it is a table of control-flow-flattened factories that build each other through a context object. They are now put back together (src/recover/moonveil-join.js): reference structure 0.2% -> 67%, fidelity 21% -> 34% on the one hand-made reference. 2.1.0 samples are a bytecode VM again (a serialized program run by a new interpreter whose outer function takes two parameters and whose inner takes none); the VM reader's first check, written for 2.0.25, stops there ("the interpreter does not have the expected shape")

backlog.item: Luraph version from structure, without a banner
backlog.detail: leave-one-out over the 198 labelled files of the public collection: the era (13 and earlier / 14.0-14.3 / 14.4-14.5 / 14.6-14.9 / 15+) is named correctly 78% of the time, the exact version 37%, the major.minor 51%.
